metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is predominantly negative (≥ 3 consecutive -1.00), model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive (e.g., -1 → +1), model delays correction; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently overestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon; apply 1–3% downward bias if recent 10-day average is > 75% of 30-day average.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model over-optimistic; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 7–10 days unless event-driven.
- If true outcome shows “rebound after dip” (e.g., 70→75→80), model often misses the rebound; add +1–3% to forecast for next 3–5 days if sentiment is positive.
- Model underestimates volatility in sentiment-driven markets; increase forecast variance by 1–2% if sentiment swings > 2x in 5-day window.
